title: Exact adapter switching with canonical prefix-cache reuse
hypothesis: A known adapter-induced right transform of K/V can represent eight specialist prefix caches as one shared canonical cache plus view coordinates, exactly matching materialized specialist attention; cache-map work should amortize at a dwell length proportional to prefix length, while direct standard-LoRA cache reuse should be inaccurate for these prefix-active specialists.
physical_object: one base-model canonical K/V prefix cache
mirror_coordinate: per-specialist known K/V orthogonal transform coordinates applied to query and attention output on switch
logical_multiplicity: eight prefix-active adapter specialists sharing one physical prefix cache
controls: direct standard-LoRA cache reuse without translation
aLoRA-style adapter activation after invocation point

development.selection_metric: attention-output relative error, actual serialized cache bytes, and transform MAC/dwell break-even

paid_objects: independent control's full per-specialist K/V caches

success_gate: Across all audit seeds: translated attention output relative error <=1e-5; shared cache payload <=25% independent cache bytes; transform-only compute break-even matches the preregistered prefix-length formula within integer rounding. Mirror-specific attribution additionally requires beating native direct rotation coordinates.
failure_gate: Any audit seed has translated error >1e-5, shared payload >25%, or no cache-state reduction. Exact native rotation alias is FAIL for Mirror-specific attribution regardless of cache algebra success.
boundaries: Synthetic single-attention-layer cache algebra only; no adapter-trained neural model, language quality, GPU, TTFT, or production serving claim.
aLoRA comparison is limited to prefix activation semantics: it preserves base prefix outputs and therefore does not realize a prefix-active specialist.
Fresh seeds and dwell values frozen before measurements; no audit tuning.
